title: Inbox consumption deletes a continuation binding before the ship lands, so any recovery that replays the change without ship's commit loses the pointer
problem: consumeCommittedItems moves each item into consumed/ with a released_continuations pointer, then deletes the root-owned registry binding (releaseBindingForConsume) before integrate runs. When integrate then fails with GIT_FLEET_REBASE_NEEDED, the only copy of the pointer lives in the failed ship commit. ADR-0105 B1 replays the audited tree without that commit, so a re-ship finds no binding and the item lands without its pointer. B1 therefore has to decline whenever a consumed item carries one. Found by the B1 architect review on 2026-09-26.
fix: Release the registry binding only after a successful integrate and push, keeping the in-commit pointer as today. Then a failed landing leaves the binding in the registry, a re-ship re-reads it, and B1 can drop its decline.
acceptance: A ship that fails at integrate leaves the continuation binding in the registry.
A re-ship after recovery writes released_continuations into the consumed item again.
A successful landing still removes the binding (the park-consume-releases-continuation-binding behaviour stays).
